message.content:
You are verifying a Node.js (ESM, .mjs) port of a Python script.

REFERENCE (ground truth, run it, do NOT modify):
  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a <hrp> --b <witver> --c <comma-separated ints>
  Source: /workspace/dataset/test4.py  (argparse: --a str required, --b int required, --c str required;
  witprog = list(map(int, args.c.split(','))); result = bech32.encode(args.a, args.b, witprog); print(result))
  The bundled Python "bech32" package internals are NOT viewable - treat it as a black box.

PORT UNDER TEST (read it, do NOT edit it):
  /output/test4.mjs  plus  /output/lib/py/*.mjs  and  /output/lib/bech32/*.mjs
  Run as: node /output/test4.mjs --a bc --b 5 --c 1,2,3

DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS (already written, use it):
  /tmp/difftest.mjs exports  runAll(cases, {label})  where cases is an array of argv arrays.
  It compares stdout, stderr (with [PYI-<pid>:ERROR] normalized) and exit code, and prints
  "[label] pass=N/M fail=K" followed by up to 20 MISMATCH blocks.
  Write your own generator script in /tmp/<yourname>.mjs like:
    import { runAll } from '/tmp/difftest.mjs';
    const cases = [ ['--a','bc','--b','5','--c','1,2'], ... ];
    await runAll(cases, { label: 'mycat' });
  Set env DIFF_CONCURRENCY=6 when running (e.g. DIFF_CONCURRENCY=6 node /tmp/mine.mjs) to avoid
  thrashing, and keep each run under ~800 cases so it finishes in a couple of minutes. Split into
  several runs if you need more coverage. Every process pair costs ~120ms of wall clock.

RULES:
 - NEVER edit anything under /output. Report only. Another process applies fixes.
 - A finding counts ONLY if you actually ran both binaries and observed a difference in
   stdout, exit code, or (PID-normalized) stderr. Paste the exact argv and both observed outputs.
 - Differences purely in the PyInstaller PID number are NOT findings.
 - Report the shortest reproducing argv you can find.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (none-boundary):
Map the exact boundary between a printed address and printed "None". For a fixed
hrp 'bc' sweep witness version -40..40 crossed with program lengths 0..42 (skip length 0 if the
CLI cannot express it) using deterministic byte values, and for a few hrps ('', 'a', 'A', 'bc',
'test', 'a1b', 'x'*45, 'x'*60) sweep witver in {0,1,15,16,17} x lengths {2,19,20,21,31,32,33,40,41}.
The port must agree on every single cell. Also probe whether hrp length affects acceptance
(total address length limits) by testing hrp lengths 1..80 with 20- and 32-byte programs.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

import sys

    echo "hrplen=$hl L=$L addrlen=$(( hl + 1 + 1 + (L*8+4)/5 + 6 ))"

    echo "  port=$p"

done

content.text: All sweeps complete. Final state: the witver × length grid and all hrp variants agree except for one open defect — an hrp-length limit the port lacks.

mismatches.why: The reference bech32 build rejects any hrp longer than 83 characters (the BIP-173 HRP limit), so bech32.encode returns None. The port's bech32Decode in /output/lib/bech32/codec.mjs has no hrp-length guard, so the round-trip validation in segwit.mjs encode() succeeds and it prints the address. Boundary is exact and sharp: hrp length 83 -> address (both agree), hrp length 84 -> ref None / port address. Verified content-independent ('x'*84 and 'ab'*42 both None in ref) and program-length-independent (fails identically for --c of 2, 20, 32 and 40 bytes, i.e. total address lengths 96 through 172). Verified for every witver that would otherwise yield an address (0 with 20/32-byte programs, 1..16 with 2..40-byte programs); 100/768 cells failed in the witver -32..31 x hrplen {83,84,85} sweep, which is exactly the set of cells where a valid address would be produced. Note the guard must sit inside the decode round trip, not before bech32_encode: with hrp length 84 and --b 32 both binaries still raise IndexError from bech32_encode, so the length rejection happens strictly after encoding. Suggested fix: add `if (hrp.length > 83) return [null, null];` to bech32Decode (equivalently a `len(hrp) > 83` clause alongside the existing pos/checksum-length test).

input.notes:
SCOPE COVERED (all via /tmp/difftest.mjs against /workspace/dataset/test4_executable and node /output/test4.mjs):

- Sweep A (/tmp/nb_sweepA.mjs, /tmp/nb_sweepA2.mjs): hrp 'bc', witver -40..40 x program lengths 1..42, deterministic bytes ((i*7+3)%256) = 3402 cells. Length 0 is not expressible: --c '' yields [''] -> int('') -> ValueError in both. Final state: 3402/3402 pass, zero stdout, stderr or exit-code differences.
- Sweep B (/tmp/nb_sweepB.mjs): hrps '', 'a', 'A', 'bc', 'test', 'a1b', 'x'*45, 'x'*60 x witver {0,1,15,16,17} x lengths {2,19,20,21,31,32,33,40,41} = 360 cells. 360/360 pass.
- Sweep C (/tmp/nb_sweepC.mjs): hrp lengths 1..80 x programs {20,32} bytes x witver {0,1} = 320 cells. 320/320 pass.
- Sweep D (/tmp/nb_sweepD.mjs): 24 exotic hrps (' ', '!', '~', '\x7f', '\t', 'é', 'ü', U+00A0, 'B', 'BC', 'Bc', '1', 'a1', '11', '0', '-', '_', ':', '"', '\\', 'x'*83, 'x'*84, 'bc'*20, 'a b') x witver {0,1,16,17} x lengths {20,32,41} = 288 cells. 282/288 pass; the 6 failures are all hrp 'x'*84 (the reported finding). Non-printable/non-ASCII/mixed-case hrps all agree on None.
- Sweep E (/tmp/nb_sweepE.mjs): byte-value edges {0,1,255,256,257,-1,-256,1000,4294967296} injected at first/mid/last position x lengths {20,32} x witver {0,1,16} = 162 cells. 162/162 pass.
- Sweep F (/tmp/nb_sweepF.mjs): hrp lengths 76..100 x lengths {2,20,32,40}, witver 1 = 100 cells. Pass for hrplen <= 83, mismatch for hrplen >= 84, at every program length.
- Sweep G (/tmp/nb_sweepG.mjs): hrp lengths {83,84,85} x witver -32..31 x lengths {2,20,32,41} = 768 cells. 668 pass; the 100 failures are exactly the hrplen 84/85 cells that would produce an address.

REFERENCE BOUNDARY MAP (hrp 'bc', confirmed cell-by-cell, port now matches all of it):
- witver <= -33 or >= 32: IndexError from bech32_encode, exit 1, traceback on stderr, for every program length. (CHARSET[witver] is out of range; -32..-1 wrap via Python negative indexing.)
- witver -32..-1: always None (the wrapped character decodes back to 32+witver > 16).
- witver 0: address only for program lengths 20 and 32; None for every other length 1..42.
- witver 1..16: address for program lengths 2..40; None for lengths 1, 41, 42.
- witver 17..31: always None (data[0] > 16 on the round trip).

TOTAL ADDRESS LENGTH: the bundled bech32 does NOT enforce BIP-173's `len(bech) > 90` rule. Verified directly: hrp 'x'*50 with a 32-byte program produces a 110-character address and hrp 'x'*83 with a 40-byte program a 155-character address, both printed by the reference. The port also prints them, so this agrees. The only length rule the reference has is on the hrp itself (<= 83). This is worth stating explicitly because the obvious "missing 90-char check" hypothesis is wrong for this build and a fix that adds it would introduce a regression.

ALREADY-FIXED DEFECT OBSERVED MID-RUN (reported for the record, do not re-fix): my first sweep A run produced 714 failures - exactly the witver in {-40..-33, 32..40} x lengths 1..42 IndexError cells. stdout and exit code matched; only stderr differed, because the port's traceback printed source lines and caret anchors that the frozen build omits. Shortest repro was `--a bc --b 32 --c 1`:
  ref  stderr: "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"test4.py\", line 16, in <module>\n  File \"test4.py\", line 12, in main\n  File \"bech32/__init__.py\", line 127, in encode\n  File \"bech32/__init__.py\", line 61, in bech32_encode\nIndexError: string index out of range\n[PYI-PID:ERROR] ..."
  port stderr: same, but with "    main()" after the line-16 frame and "    result = bech32.encode(args.a, args.b, witprog)  # Encode segwit address\n             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^" after the line-12 frame.
The same shape appeared on the ValueError path (`--a bc --b 0 --c x` and `--a bc --b 0 --c ''` printed "    witprog = list(map(int, args.c.split(',')))" plus anchors that the reference omits). /output/lib/py/traceback.mjs was rewritten during my run to consult a new /output/lib/py/linecache.mjs, and I re-verified afterwards: all 3402 sweep-A cells now pass, including all 714 IndexError cells.

SUSPICIOUS BUT UNCONFIRMED (outside my remit, flagging only): the new linecache-based traceback resolves source lines from the current working directory, so behaviour on the error paths is now cwd-dependent. All my runs used cwd=/tmp where no test4.py exists. If a run happens with cwd=/workspace/dataset (which contains test4.py), both binaries would consult linecache, but whether their line/anchor output stays identical there - the file on disk has the comment banner and 16-line layout the anchors were recorded against - I did not test. I saw no difference and this is not a confirmed finding.
